title: Nivolumab · every 2 weeks · previously treated NSCLC
purpose: Aim to control advanced lung cancer, relieve symptoms and prolong life where possible.
context_label: Previously treated locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
indication_text: Adults with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC after prior chemotherapy; recurrence or progression during or after one prior platinum-containing doublet for advanced/metastatic disease; ECOG 0–1.
schedule_summary: Nivolumab 240 mg IV over 30 minutes OR 600 mg as a subcutaneous injection over 3–5 minutes on Day 1 every 2 weeks. Your team confirms one formulation; the whole visit includes checks and preparation. Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity, with individual benefit and safety review.
administration_text: Nivolumab 240 mg IV over 30 minutes OR 600 mg as a subcutaneous injection over 3–5 minutes on Day 1 every 2 weeks. Your team confirms one formulation; the whole visit includes checks and preparation.
monitoring_summary: Blood count, kidney/liver tests and glucose before every 2-week cycle; thyroid once a month; cortisol if clinically indicated. Review cancer progression before cycle 8. Continue immune-toxicity monitoring for at least 5 months after the last dose.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab blocks PD-1 on immune cells, helping them recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause inflammation in healthy organs.
agents.watch: Report new breathing, bowel, skin, hormone, heart or nerve symptoms promptly; these may be immune inflammation.
risks: Immune inflammation of lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, hormone glands, skin, heart and nervous system
Some effects need steroids, hospital care or long-term hormone replacement
Effects may start after the final dose

urgent_extra: Contact the oncology team immediately for new or worsening breathlessness, chest pain, persistent diarrhoea, severe tummy pain, yellow skin/eyes, much less urine, severe headache, marked weakness, confusion, unusual thirst or passing much more urine, or a spreading/blistering rash. For severe breathing difficulty, collapse, seizure or other immediately dangerous symptoms, seek emergency care. Do not wait for the next infusion.
consent_support: Discuss the aim for your exact lung setting, likely benefit, alternatives, important immune risks and how treatment may be paused or stopped. Some side effects need long-term medicines. Ask about fertility, pregnancy, breastfeeding and effects on daily life.
safety_note: Immune effects can happen on any day and after treatment ends. Carry your immunotherapy alert card and tell any healthcare team that you receive nivolumab.

day_groups.title: Your treatment visit
day_groups.body: The team checks blood results, symptoms and medicines before the prescribed infusion or injection. Tell the nurse immediately about itching, flushing, breathlessness, dizziness or feeling suddenly unwell.
day_groups.action: Before leaving, confirm the next tests, treatment visit and urgent contact number.

day_groups.title: Between visits
day_groups.body: You may feel well between infusions, but immune inflammation can begin at any time. Keep a short symptom record and take medicines exactly as prescribed. Contact your team about new symptoms instead of waiting for your next appointment.
day_groups.action: Confirm monthly thyroid tests and who arranges them; report new symptoms without waiting for the next treatment.

support.title: Sickness medicines
support.text: Nivolumab alone has minimal sickness risk. Routine preventive anti-sickness medicines or premedication are not usually required; the team may prescribe symptom relief.

support.title: Immune alert card
support.text: Carry your alert card during treatment and afterwards. Show it when seeking urgent care; symptoms can be mistaken for an infection or an ordinary stomach upset.

support.title: Hormones and steroids
support.text: Some immune effects need steroids or hormone replacement. Follow the prescribed plan and do not stop steroids suddenly. Ask for help if symptoms worsen or you cannot take essential medicines. Hormone replacement alone does not always mean nivolumab must stop. Your team checks symptoms and recovery and reviews any medicines that suppress the immune system before deciding whether treatment can continue or restart.

support.title: Pregnancy and breastfeeding
support.text: Discuss pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding before treatment. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 5 months after the last dose. Breastfeeding requires a specialist decision; contact your team promptly if pregnancy occurs.

questions.a: Previously treated locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). It is used after previous chemotherapy to help control cancer; ask how the benefits and alternatives apply to you.

questions.a: Nivolumab 240 mg IV over 30 minutes OR 600 mg as a subcutaneous injection over 3–5 minutes on Day 1 every 2 weeks. Your team confirms one formulation; the whole visit includes checks and preparation.

questions.q: Who arranges my tests and scans?
questions.a: Blood count, kidney/liver tests and glucose before every 2-week cycle; thyroid once a month; cortisol if clinically indicated. Review cancer progression before cycle 8. Continue immune-toxicity monitoring for at least 5 months after the last dose.

questions.q: When should I call the team?
questions.a: Report new breathlessness, persistent diarrhoea, severe pain, yellow eyes, reduced urine, severe headache, weakness, unusual thirst or a spreading/blistering rash immediately. Use your oncology contact plan; severe breathing difficulty, collapse, seizure or severe chest pain needs emergency care.
Ask about other anticancer treatment, trials and symptom-focused care suited to your cancer and preferences. Support remains available if you decline treatment.

New cough or breathlessness can signal inflammation or another urgent cause.
Chest pain, racing heartbeat or fainting needs urgent assessment.
Yellow eyes/skin or dark urine may signal inflammation; tests also check the liver.
Report much less urine, new swelling or a change in kidney tests.
New or persistent diarrhoea, blood in stools or severe tummy pain needs urgent advice.
Spreading rash, blisters, severe weakness or muscle pain needs prompt review.

scope_note: Previously treated locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This patient suite is lung-focused; other shared protocol indications need their own counselling.

evidence.title: Why this treatment may be offered
evidence.intro: Nivolumab can help the immune system control some previously treated lung cancers. Some people benefit for a long time; others do not benefit.
evidence.interpretation: Trial results describe groups, not an individual prognosis.
evidence.population: Previously treated locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
evidence.limitations: CheckMate 017/057 studied nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks versus docetaxel, after platinum. Fixed-dose q14/q28 and SC schedules are supported through dosing/formulation bridging, not separate randomised superiority estimates. The pooled lung results do not establish benefit for other tumours or first-line, perioperative or small-cell lung settings.

items.title: Treatment aim
items.text: Aim to control advanced lung cancer, relieve symptoms and prolong life where possible.

items.title: Choices
items.text: Discuss other treatment, trials and symptom-focused care with your team.

items.title: PD-1 blockade
items.text: Nivolumab blocks PD-1 on immune cells, helping them recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause the immune system to inflame healthy organs.

items.title: Healthy organs
items.text: Inflammation can affect lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, skin, glands, muscles, heart and nerves. Some effects are serious, delayed or permanent.

chapters.title: Your treatment course
chapters.intro: Confirm the formulation with your team.

items.title: Administration
items.text: Nivolumab 240 mg IV over 30 minutes OR 600 mg as a subcutaneous injection over 3–5 minutes on Day 1 every 2 weeks. Your team confirms one formulation; the whole visit includes checks and preparation.

items.title: Course length
items.text: Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity, with individual benefit and safety review.

items.title: Pauses
items.text: Treatment may be held or stopped for side effects. Nivolumab is not routinely dose-reduced. Tell the team about missed appointments.

items.title: Previous permanent-stop decisions
items.text: If your team has permanently stopped nivolumab because of a serious immune reaction, improvement does not automatically make restarting safe. Keep that decision in your treatment record; only your specialist team can review further treatment.
